results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Required] [Prerequisite]: Validate base and head refs exist and are accessible using GITHUB_GET_A_BRANCH (repeat per ref; use owner-qualified head when applicable).
[Optional (if ref name is uncertain)] [Prerequisite]: Discover candidate branch names using GITHUB_LIST_BRANCHES (use to correct typos/format before write ops).
[Optional (to prevent no-diff/unrelated-history failures)] [Prerequisite]: Compare base vs head using GITHUB_COMPARE_TWO_COMMITS (proceed only if head is ahead / not identical).
[Optional (to avoid duplicate-PR failures)] [Prerequisite]: Check for an existing open PR for the same head/base using GITHUB_FIND_PULL_REQUESTS (keep query tightly repository-scoped).
[Required] [Step]: Get final confirmation, then create the pull request using GITHUB_CREATE_A_PULL_REQUEST (set base, head, title/body; draft if needed).
[Required] [Next Step]: Retrieve PR number/state and link using GITHUB_GET_A_PULL_REQUEST (record response.data.number and response.data.html_url).
[Optional (if metadata/state needs adjustment)] [Next Step]: Edit title/body/draft/base/closed state using GITHUB_UPDATE_A_PULL_REQUEST, then re-check using GITHUB_GET_A_PULL_REQUEST.

[Fallback (if creation fails with 422/403/404)] [Fallback]: Re-validate refs/access using GITHUB_GET_A_BRANCH (and GITHUB_LIST_BRANCHES if naming is unclear), then retry using GITHUB_CREATE_A_PULL_REQUEST.
known_pitfalls: [GITHUB_CREATE_A_PULL_REQUEST] HTTP 422 Validation Failed if base/head invalid/identical, no common history, or an open PR already exists; errors[].field may be "head" with code="invalid"; can also fail with HTTP 403 due to access restrictions.
[GITHUB_CREATE_A_PULL_REQUEST] Create response payload can be very large/truncated; rely on response.data.number and response.data.html_url as canonical outputs.
[GITHUB_GET_A_PULL_REQUEST] Immediately after creation, mergeable may be null and mergeable_state may be "unknown"; rapid follow-up GETs can transiently 404.
[GITHUB_GET_A_BRANCH] May return HTTP 403 when access for an app is restricted; downstream PR create/read checks will fail until access is approved.
[GITHUB_FIND_PULL_REQUESTS] Unscoped searches can return an enormous result set and oversized responses; keep filters tight and expect minimal/optimized fields unless explicitly expanded.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Filter and sort pull request list results by an actor field
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
prs=response_data.get('pull_requests',[])
actor='a_user'
filtered=[p for p in prs if p.get('user',{}).get('login')==actor]
filtered.sort(key=lambda p:p.get('created_at',''))
rows=[(p.get('title'),p.get('created_at')) for p in filtered]
```

GITHUB_CREATE_A_PULL_REQUEST.description: Creates a pull request in a GitHub repository, requiring existing `base` and `head` branches; `title` or `issue` must be provided.

base.description: The name of the branch you want the changes pulled into. This must be an existing branch on the current (target) repository. You cannot submit a pull request to one repository that requests a merge to a base branch of another repository.

examples: This PR introduces a new feature that does X, Y, and Z.
Fixes #42 by addressing the off-by-one error.
body.description: The detailed description or contents of the pull request.

head.description: The name of the branch where your changes are implemented. IMPORTANT: This branch must already exist in the repository (or fork) before calling this action. You must first create the branch and push commits to it (using git or the 'Create a reference' action), then create the PR. For cross-repository pull requests, namespace `head` with the source owner and branch, like `username:branch`.

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

draft.description: Indicates whether the pull request should be created as a draft. Draft pull requests cannot be merged until marked as ready for review.

issue.description: The number of an existing issue in the repository to convert into a pull request. If provided, the issue's title and body may be used for the pull request. Required if `title` is not specified.

owner.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

title.description: The title of the new pull request. Required unless `issue` is specified.

head_repo.description: The name of the repository (e.g., 'octocat/Hello-World') where the changes in the pull request were made. This field is required for cross-repository pull requests if both the source and target repositories are owned by the same organization but are different repositories.

maintainer_can_modify.description: Indicates whether maintainers of the upstream repository can modify the pull request. This is primarily relevant for pull requests originating from forks.

GITHUB_GET_A_BRANCH.description: Retrieves detailed information for a specified branch within a GitHub repository.

repo.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

owner.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

branch.description: The name of the branch. Cannot contain wildcard characters. To use wildcard characters in branch names, use [the GraphQL API](https://docs.github.com/graphql). If 'HEAD' is provided, it will be resolved to the repository's default branch.

GITHUB_FIND_PULL_REQUESTS.description: Primary tool to find and search pull requests. Supports filtering by repository, author, state, labels, and merge status, and returns structured PR data for reliable use in workflows. GitHub search results are capped at ~1000 total items; narrow filters when totals approach this limit. `created_since`/`updated_since` filter on creation/update timestamps, not `merged_at`; apply merge-date filtering client-side.

page.description: Page number of results to fetch.

repo.description: Filter by specific repository. Can be provided in 'owner/repo' format (e.g., 'facebook/react'), or as just the repo name when used with the owner parameter. When owner and repo are both provided and have the same value, they are combined as 'owner/repo'. When omitted along with owner, search scope is determined by for_authenticated_user flag. The repository must exist and be accessible with your token. Prefer 'owner/repo' format; bare repo name without the `owner` parameter causes invalid repository format errors.

sort.description: Field to sort results by. Set explicitly to 'updated' with `order=desc` when recency matters; default behavior may return best-match relevance ordering instead.

owner.description: Filter by repository owner (user or organization). Can be used alone to search all repositories for an owner, or combined with repo parameter to specify owner and repo separately. When both owner and repo are provided, the search is scoped to 'owner/repo'. When omitted along with repo, search scope is determined by for_authenticated_user flag. The owner must exist and repositories must be accessible with your token.

query.description: Optional search query for PR title, description, or commit messages. Supports GitHub search syntax including label filters (e.g., 'label:bug'), logical operators (AND, OR, NOT), and text search. If not provided, PRs will be listed based on other filter parameters. Type qualifiers (type:pr, is:pr, is:issue, type:issue) are automatically normalized. When using logical operators with qualifiers like labels, the query is automatically grouped for proper parsing. When omitting query, ensure at least one structured filter parameter is provided; passing no query and no filters may cause validation errors. Prefer dedicated parameters (`label`, `state`, `author`) over embedding qualifiers in the query string. Exact title matching is not supported; post-filter on title client-side if needed.

author.description: Filter by PR author username. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.

assignee.description: Filter by PR assignee username. Use '@me' for current user. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.

mentions.description: Filter by username mentioned in PR. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.

per_page.description: Number of results per page (maximum 100). GitHub caps total search results at ~1000 items; iterate `page` until results fewer than `per_page` are returned, and add `repo`, `label`, or date filters when totals approach 1000.

is_merged.description: Filter by merge status. True for merged PRs, False for unmerged, None for all.

created_since.description: Filter PRs created after this date (ISO 8601 format). Provide as UTC ISO 8601 timestamp to avoid off-by-one-day errors at range boundaries. Does not filter on `merged_at`.

updated_since.description: Filter PRs updated after this date (ISO 8601 format).

response_detail.description: Level of detail in the response. 'minimal' (default) returns an optimized response for AI agents. 'full' returns the complete GitHub API response.

for_authenticated_user.description: Include private repositories accessible to the authenticated user in search results. When True without repo/owner, searches PRs involving you (author, assignee, mentions, commenter) across all accessible repos. When False without repo/owner, restricts to public repos only. When repo/owner is specified, this flag has no effect on scope. Set to True when searching private repositories; False searches all of GitHub and produces large noisy result sets.
